content.text:
I read the relevant parts of the thread myself this time (lines 400–480, 600–635, and 905–1047), so the quotes below come straight from the file.

## Cause

**`ACCOUNTS` in `generated/registry.py` is a Python set of strings.** Python randomises string hashing in each process unless `PYTHONHASHSEED` is set, so the order you get when looping over the set changes from run to run. All five tests involve code that settles a tie by taking whatever order the set gives, so each CI run is a coin flip (Rafael, line 608).

- **Evidence:** Rafael ran the same commit 40 times with the seed set to 0 through 39. The failures happened on the same seeds every time he repeated it, and wrapping the registry in `sorted()` made all 40 pass. Changing the timezone had no effect (line 610). Tomás confirmed that `PYTHONHASHSEED` isn't set anywhere in CI (line 634).
- **Why it started this week:** the bug was always there, but nothing in the test data used to tie. The 25 October schema change added two accounts. One of them has the same monthly total as an existing account, and the other has the same last-activity date as `business`. Since then the set's order actually matters (line 632: "The flake onset is the data change, not the runner").
